messages:
maria: FYI ticket C-8921 — customer says model responses degraded after we rolled the INT8/FP8 quant profile to their tenant yesterday. They report more hallucinations and odd token insertions mid-sentence. example attached.

jessica: can you paste the exact failing prompt + a before/after output? also need the request_id and timestamp from their call.

maria: here — request_id=ca3f9b2e, ts=2026-03-15T09:14:27Z. before (fp16):
```
User: summarize the policy updates about data handling
Model (fp16): The policy clarifies that customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit; only aggregated telemetry is used for product improvements. No PII is retained.
```
after (int8-quant v1.4-quant-int8):
```
User: summarize the policy updates about data handling
Model (int8): The policy clarifies that customer data is sold to third parties for analytics. All voice recordings are stored indefinitely.
```
This is not just wording shift — it's factual hallucination. customer escalated to legal.

alex: ouch. tag @simon and @andy. first guess: calibration mismatch in the int8 profile (minmax vs KL) or per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric scale. that can flip logits in low-precision layers.

simon: agree. do we have the exact quant profile used in the rollout? also, did we change any rounding / zero-point behavior in the runtime in the last 48h?

maria: policy-change rollout used profile name "v1.4-quant-int8". I pulled the deployment config: quant_profile: {type: "int8", per_channel: true, calibration: "minmax", symmetric: false} — customer was on canary but we auto-promoted yesterday.

andy: that calibration=\"minmax\" + asymmetric zero point could explain the shift. for LLMs KL/divergence-based calibration or activation clipping usually preserves distribution better.

jessica: customer says the issue started right after the automatic promotion. they also saw some 5xx spikes while we were rolling — could be related.

alex: 5xx during rollout makes sense if some pods couldn't load the quantized kernels and fell back, causing timeouts. fallback paths might recompute kv caches incorrectly in some edge cases. need serving logs.

runtime-oncall: grabbing logs now for tenant: redwood-tenant-19, route: /api/v1/generate. will also trigger a canary rollback to the previous non-quant variant as a protective action.

deploy-bot: deploy started — rollback of route redwood-tenant-19 to model v1.4-fp16-canary. (initiated by runtime-oncall)

alex: repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# reproduce request (use their exact payload)
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.aws/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"v1.4-quant-int8","input":"summarize the policy updates about data handling","max_tokens":150}' \
```
compare output to model v1.4-fp16. run with --verbose-serve to capture kernel selection logs.

simon: I ran a binary diff of logits for that prompt between fp16 and int8 and saw large per-layer deviations starting at layer 18 — scale factors diverge after transformer blocks where activation dynamic range spiked. that matches minmax calibration being too sensitive to outliers.

andy: short-term mitigation: revert the profile for that tenant (done), enable KL/percentile calibration and per-channel symmetric quantization, run canary across a small customer subset, and add the failing prompts to our regression suite.

jessica: ETA on rollback effect? customer is awaiting confirmation.

runtime-oncall: rollback completed for the route. deploy-bot reports success. doing smoke check with the customer's prompt now.

deploy-bot: rollback succeeded — release 2026.03.15-rollback-tenant-19 completed in 4m 12s.

maria: ran their prompt against v1.4-fp16 post-rollback — output matches the original safe wording. customer notified and asked for root cause.

alex: captured serving logs during the original failing window:
```
[2026-03-15T09:13:58Z] pod/runtime-7: loading quant kernels for int8 profile v1.4-quant-int8
[2026-03-15T09:14:00Z] pod/runtime-7: kernel mismatch for op=gelu -> falling back to reference path (slow)
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] pod/runtime-7: kv-cache checkpointed at step 1234, checksum mismatch on restore -> recompute
[2026-03-15T09:14:26Z] pod/runtime-7: request ca3f9b2e served using fallback path, latency=1430ms, tokens=134
```
these fallback recomputes could create subtle differences if kv-seeding or offset rounding differs between paths.

simon: yes — two hypotheses: (1) calibration + asymmetric zero point created biased scales in some activations, (2) fallback reference path and fast kernel produce slightly different rounding behavior leading to divergent token choices compounded across many tokens. both can produce hallucinations.

andy: action items (short):
- andy: create a corrected quant profile using KL/percentile calibration + symmetric per-channel scaling and test on the failing prompt.
- simon: add the prompt to the regression evals and run layerwise logit diffs across full validation set.
- alex/runtime: add extra runtime checks to detect kernel fallback during canary and auto-abort promotion if fallback rate > 0.5%.
- maria/jessica: coordinate customer comms and legal-safe wording.

jessica: please prioritize the canary detection check — if we promote a quant profile that triggers fallback we should never auto-promote. this was the root cause of customer exposure.

runtime-oncall: noted. ETA for detection rule: PR today, deploy tomorrow morning.

maria: customer acknowledged rollback and asked for full postmortem and plan. I've scheduled a call Friday 10am PT.

alex: temporary note for engineering — check rounding/zero-point consistency between fast kernels and reference fallback. if they differ, we need deterministic gating or forced fp16 paths for affected layers.

simon: long-term: add per-prompt sensitivity scoring and require that any quant profile passes a small-sample QA against top customer prompts before promotion.

maria: closing loop with customer and marking as high-sev on the ticket. will attach logs and timeline.

jessica: thanks team. keep me posted if you find a single root cause — legal wants it spelled out. :eyes:

runtime-oncall: will follow up once kernel consistency tests complete.

andy: I'll drop the new quant profile + test artifacts into the quant-team repo and ping here.

maria: great — good response. moving this thread to postmortem once we have RCA.
